note: Manually crosschecked factual runtime behavior against Rust source in isolated Worldkiln AI copy. Facts are limited; not a proof of every API.

facts.fact: Any enabled standalone .aeo file in scripts/ runs its top-level statements when Play starts. It does not require an entity declaration or an event wrapper.
Disabled script paths are skipped by the initial top-level scheduler. Re-enabling spawns a new top-level task if one is not already scheduled.

facts.topic: actor attached script module parent self.parent
facts.fact: When a .aeo Module is attached to an authored Actor through the project hierarchy/binding, it runs as a distinct Actor Module instance, not a standalone global script. self.parent resolves to that Actor. The same file can have separate instances per Actor.

facts.topic: actor attached scripts entity lifecycle differences
facts.fact: Actor Modules DO NOT bind legacy entity {...} blocks. Entity declaration lifecycle methods in an Actor Module are not invoked as Actor callbacks; instead use top-level Module statements and assign supported Actor handler fields. No fn on_ready lifecycle assumed for Actor Module.
facts.example:
const actor = self.parent
actor.on_touch = fn(thing) { debug.log("Touched", thing) }

facts.fact: A standalone Module instance has no Actor parent; attempting to read self.parent throws an interpreter error. Do not emit self.parent unless the Module has a known Actor attachment.

facts.topic: cell bound script entity declaration binding cell
facts.fact: The current Cell script binding path is separate from Actor Modules: a Cell binding uses Cell ID and script path and checks for a matching legacy entity declaration before starting its lifecycle. Do NOT assume self.parent resolves to a Cell: current Module self.parent logic explicitly handles Actor IDs only.

facts.topic: legacy entity script lifecycle cell on_spawn on_ready update on_destroy
facts.fact: The Entity lifecycle supports on_spawn(), on_ready(), update(dt), and on_destroy() only when a compatible Entity declaration is actually bound/instantiated. An unbound declaration alone does not trigger any lifecycle method.

facts.topic: event listener on start custom event.fire
facts.fact: on name(args) { ... } is an event listener registration. It does NOT automatically run at startup merely because it is named start. Event dispatch must occur. Top-level statements are the ordinary startup mechanism.

facts.topic: ui.new ui.find ui.get ui.delete ui.get_viewport_size UI script
facts.fact: Worldkiln exposes runtime UI functions ui.new(type), ui.find(key), ui.get(key), ui.delete(handle), and ui.get_viewport_size(). Inspect stdlib.rs for arguments; UI controls are handles.

facts.topic: menu ui Panel Text Button Image Video
facts.fact: Current engine UI runtime types include Panel, Text, Button, Image and Video; live /aeoscript/ui/ page lists only Panel, Text, Button and is behind current source for media controls.

facts.topic: editor authored UI project saved document versus runtime UI
facts.fact: Worldkiln has a persisted authored UI workspace with documents (default Main UI, key main_ui). UI created at runtime and modified during Play is not automatically saved back to authored UI. Main menu design may require editor-owned UI document changes plus runtime AeoScript.
Files under playerscripts/ attach as Player modules and are not executed as standalone global scripts; use the Player context and explicit module handles.
AeoScript syntax is owned by the Rust Lexer and Parser. Syntax acceptance is not proof that a runtime method exists, a binding exists, or a handler is dispatched.

facts.topic: documentation physics entity parser property reserved keyword entity
facts.fact: Three live documentation examples fail current lexer/parser because they access .entity as a member, where 'entity' is a reserved token. They occur in the Entity and Physics API reference pages. Do not use these examples unmodified.

facts.topic: Project Manager Project Explorer attach parent script actor hierarchy drag drop
facts.fact: Scripts are NOT automatically parented to Actors or Cells when created. A creator parents or moves script nodes in the Project Manager/Project Explorer hierarchy. Actor attachment is derived from the nearest non-Folder Actor ancestor. A script nested beneath another script is not separately attached. Moving a script beneath an Actor creates/synchronizes its ActorScriptBinding; moving it out removes that binding. The editor uses atomic hierarchy move validation, undo snapshots, binding reconciliation, and project save-dirty tracking. The AI must not claim it has parented a script unless it has executed the same editor hierarchy mutation and binding synchronization; source generation alone does not parent anything.
